name: Netlify
verdict: Self-serve: create an OAuth app under your user settings and send users to Netlify's authorize page, likely in 1-3 days. No review is documented, though the current docs could not be fully confirmed.
needGuide: Short one: create the OAuth app, add redirect URIs, and verify grant types against current docs.

auth.detail: Docs say to use OAuth2 applications for public integrations and personal access tokens (PATs) for your own scripts. Authorization endpoint is https://app.netlify.com/authorize. Netlify's own tutorial uses the implicit flow (response_type=token, token in URL hash); a 2016 blog post suggests the authorization code grant when you have a server. Token lifetime, refresh tokens and scopes are not documented in the pages read. Resetting a user's password invalidates all their PATs and OAuth tokens.

approval.gate: None documented: no review, listing or partner step is described for OAuth applications; users approve on Netlify's authorize page. Netlify also runs a separate extensions/integrations program (not researched).

scopes.why: No scope model documented; tokens appear to act with the user's full API access.
scopes.summary: No scope model documented: tokens appear to act with the authorizing user's full API access (inference). Check https://open-api.netlify.com for endpoints.

prerequisites: Account and owner: The OAuth app lives in a personal user's settings, not a team, so create it from a shared company-owned Netlify user (or bot account) to avoid losing it when someone leaves. No special role documented.
Where you register: User settings → Applications → OAuth applications → New OAuth app (name, redirect URI); save Client ID and Secret

registerAt.path: User settings → Applications → OAuth applications → New OAuth app (name, redirect URI); save Client ID and Secret

steps.do: Sign in to a company-owned Netlify user and open https://app.netlify.com/user/applications#oauth-applications
Click New OAuth app; enter name and redirect URI(s) for dev and prod; save Client ID and secret
Send users to https://app.netlify.com/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type and a random state; verify state on return
Prefer a server-side callback so the token is never exposed to the browser; store tokens encrypted
Call https://api.netlify.com/api/v1 with Authorization: Bearer and a User-Agent header containing a contact email
Test with a second Netlify account, including revoke and SAML-team cases

roles.team: The OAuth app lives in a personal user's settings, not a team, so create it from a shared company-owned Netlify user (or bot account) to avoid losing it when someone leaves. No special role documented.
roles.console: none documented (apps are per user; no collaborator feature found)
roles.customer: The end user authorizes the app on the Netlify consent page. Teams that require SAML SSO deny PATs by default; whether OAuth tokens need the same SAML opt-in was not confirmed. Team owners may be needed for team-level access (likely).

testing: Register an app under your own Netlify account (free) and authorize with a second test account; use a localhost redirect URI such as http://localhost:8888/ for netlify dev.

blockers.problem: Implicit flow returns the token in the URL hash
blockers.fix: Use a server and authorization code where possible; confirm the grant is accepted for your app.

blockers.problem: No documented token lifetime or refresh
blockers.fix: Handle 401s by sending the user through authorization again.
Ask the customer admin to allow it (PATs have an explicit SAML checkbox).

blockers.problem: Password reset by the user kills all tokens

automation.agentCan: Write the authorize/callback code, token storage and API client, run test calls, and draft the app description.
automation.humanMust: Log in (with 2FA) and register the OAuth app in user settings, and have a customer user approve the consent screen.

uncertain: Could not confirm grant types actually supported today (code vs implicit), token lifetime, scopes, how redirect URIs are managed, or whether any extension/partner review exists.
Current OAuth reference pages failed to fetch; the 2016 blog is stale.
